correctness.rationale: Let T_j be the d=p^j term and p odd, r>=2, p∤a. For j=r, v_p(T_r)=3r-2. For 1<=j<r, m=r-j, Legendre gives v_p(T_j)-(3r-2)=j(p^m-1)+(p^m-1)/(p-1)-3m, strictly positive except (p,r,j)=(3,2,1). For j=0, v_p(T_0)=(p^r-1)/(p-1), strictly greater than 3r-2 except (p,r)=(3,2). In the exception, (T_0,T_1,T_2)/81 reduces to (a,2a,a) mod 3, sum a nonzero. Hence v_p(S)=3r-2, no hidden cancellation. Recomputed integer defining sums for 30 unit cases over p=3,5,7,11 and r=2,3, confirming but not proving the unrestricted valuation.
